description: Nebraska-only rules checked against the cited Nebraska Revised Statutes. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines.

questions.q: Unless reduced or a special hazard requires a lower speed, Nebraska's maximum in a residential district is
questions.explanation: Section 60-6,186(1)(a) sets twenty-five miles per hour in any residential district. Subsection (1)(b) sets twenty miles per hour in any business district. Those maxima may be reduced under subsection (2).

questions.q: Nebraska's maximum speed in a business district is
questions.explanation: Section 60-6,186(1)(b) sets twenty miles per hour in any business district. The residential maximum in the same section is twenty-five miles per hour.

questions.q: On Nebraska's National System of Interstate and Defense Highways, the maximum is 75 mph except
options: It is 55 mph statewide at night
It is 65 mph in Douglas County
It is 70 mph for every truck
questions.explanation: Section 60-6,186(1)(i) sets seventy-five miles per hour on the National System of Interstate and Defense Highways, except sixty-five miles per hour for any portion of that system in Douglas County and for Interstate 180 in Lancaster County and Interstate 129 in Dakota County.

questions.q: On a Nebraska expressway or super-two highway that is part of the state highway system, the statutory maximum is
questions.explanation: Section 60-6,186(1)(g) sets seventy miles per hour upon an expressway or a super-two highway that is part of the state highway system. Subsection (1)(h) also sets seventy miles per hour on a state-system freeway that is not part of the interstate system.

questions.q: Nebraska makes it unlawful to operate or be in actual physical control of a motor vehicle at an alcohol concentration of
options: 0.05 gram or more per 100 milliliters of blood
0.08 gram or more per 100 milliliters of blood
0.10 gram or more per 100 milliliters of blood
0.02 gram or more for every driver
questions.explanation: Section 60-6,196(1) prohibits operating or being in actual physical control while under the influence, or with eight-hundredths of one gram or more by weight of alcohol per one hundred milliliters of blood, or per two hundred ten liters of breath.

questions.q: For a Nebraska driver under 21, it is unlawful to operate a motor vehicle at an alcohol concentration of
questions.explanation: Section 60-6,211.01 makes it unlawful for a person under twenty-one to operate or be in actual physical control with two-hundredths of one gram or more by weight of alcohol per one hundred milliliters of blood, or per two hundred ten liters of breath, but less than the concentration in section 60-6,196.

questions.q: A Nebraska commercial-motor-vehicle operator whose blood or breath test discloses an alcohol concentration of 0.04 or more
options: Is treated the same as a result below 0.02
Must be placed out of service for twenty-four hours
Loses the CDL for life on the first result
questions.explanation: Section 60-4,164(5) says a person operating or in actual physical control of a commercial motor vehicle who submits to a test disclosing four-hundredths of one gram or more per one hundred milliliters of blood, or per two hundred ten liters of breath, shall be placed out of service for twenty-four hours, and the officer shall forward a sworn report to the director.

questions.q: Nebraska's director shall revoke an operator's license when the record shows
options: 12 or more points within two years
6 points in 12 months for any driver
questions.explanation: Section 60-4,183 says that whenever any person has accumulated a total of twelve or more points within any period of two years, as set out in section 60-4,182, the director shall summarily revoke the operator's license. The same section states the revocation is for six months from the later of the signing of the order or release from the named confinement, unless the abstract directed a longer period.

questions.q: For ordinary Nebraska speeding that is more than 5 mph but not more than 10 mph over the limit, the point value is
questions.explanation: Section 60-4,182(10)(a) assigns 2 points for speeding more than five miles per hour but not more than ten miles per hour over the speed limit. A separate scale in subdivision (10)(b) applies to the higher limits in section 60-6,186(1)(f) through (i).

questions.q: Nebraska may issue an LPD-learner's permit to a person who is at least
questions.explanation: Section 60-4,123(1) says any person who is at least fifteen years of age may apply for an LPD-learner's permit. The written examination may be taken beginning sixty days before the fifteenth birthday, but the permit is not issued until age fifteen. The permit is valid for twelve months.

questions.q: A Nebraska provisional operator's permit holder, unless an exception applies, may drive only
options: At any hour during the first year
questions.explanation: Section 60-4,120.01(3)(a) limits a provisional operator's permit holder to the period beginning at 6 a.m. and ending at 12 midnight, except when en route between the residence and a place of employment or a school activity. The holder may drive at any hour if accompanied by a parent, guardian, or adult at least twenty-one who has a current Nebraska license or is licensed in another state.

questions.q: In Nebraska, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: Nebraska requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 6 months.

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in Nebraska complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: Nebraska requires 50 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.

provenance.manual: Provisional Operator’s Permit (POP) | Nebraska Department of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: Of a Nebraska teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: Nebraska requires at least 10 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.

provenance.manual: Provisional Operator’s Permit (POP) | Nebraska Department of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: In Nebraska, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Nebraska, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16 years.

provenance.manual: Provisional Operator’s Permit (POP) | Nebraska Department of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: During which hours may a newly licensed teen in Nebraska not drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: Nebraska restricts provisional drivers from Midnight to 6 a.m., with exceptions such as work or school.

provenance.manual: Provisional Operator’s Permit (POP) | Nebraska Department of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: In Nebraska, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: Nebraska drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 17 years.

questions.q: How many questions are on the Nebraska car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: The Nebraska car knowledge test has 25 questions.

provenance.manual: Driver Licensing Examiner Manual (Class O Written Test)

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Nebraska car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 80% to pass the Nebraska car knowledge test.

provenance.manual: Driver Licensing Examiner Manual (Class O Written Test)

questions.q: In Nebraska, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in Nebraska brings a suspension of 1 year.

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Nebraska?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Nebraska can be posted up to 75 mph for cars.

questions.q: Which best describes Nebraska's law on drivers using a phone?
options: Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
Only texting is banned for all drivers
No statewide ban on phone use or texting
Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
questions.explanation: Nebraska: only texting is banned for all drivers.

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in Nebraska?
options: Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In Nebraska, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: only from a one-way street onto a one-way street.

questions.q: How is Nebraska's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
No seat belt law for adults
questions.explanation: Nebraska seat belt enforcement is secondary.

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in Nebraska?
questions.explanation: Nebraska requires a car seat or booster until 8 years, with height or weight exceptions.

questions.q: What is Nebraska's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Nebraska requires at least $25,000 / $50,000 / $25,000.

questions.q: Under Nebraska's point system, what is the lowest point total that can suspend an adult's license?
questions.explanation: Nebraska can suspend an adult's license at 12 points in 24 months.
